result.summary: This PR fixes a bug where MiniMiner's calculateIndividualBumpFees returns an empty map when it cannot compute bump fees for a large unconfirmed transaction cluster, causing wallet code to index into the map and surface an internal std::out_of_range/map::at style failure to users. It changes AvailableCoins to return util::Result<CoinsResult> so the error can propagate cleanly through transaction creation, sendall, and listunspent, and adds a functional regression test plus fuzz/unit coverage for the failure path.
result.problem: Wallets with more than ~500 unconfirmed ancestor transactions selected as inputs get a nondescript internal error instead of a clear message when the wallet tries to compute bump fees, as described in issue #29711. This affects any user or application funding transactions from a large unconfirmed input set.

resolved_concerns: achow101 suggested avoiding an optional<>-based interface change and keeping the map; author reworked it accordingly.
achow101 argued AvailableCoins should propagate errors via util::Result<CoinsResult> rather than an ad hoc mechanism; author implemented this in the 2026-08-19 push.

No maintainer ACK has landed yet on the final (2026-08-19) design, so it's unclear how strongly the project wants this exact approach versus alternatives like extending CoinsResult with error state as achow101 first floated.
result.card: This PR fixes a bug where MiniMiner's bump-fee calculation can silently fail (returning an empty map) when a wallet's unconfirmed input set exceeds MiniMiner's cluster limit, causing wallet funding and sendall to index into the map and leak a nondescript internal exception to users, per issue #29711. It changes AvailableCoins to return util::Result<CoinsResult> so the failure propagates as a clear wallet error, and adds a functional regression test plus fuzz/unit coverage. The single reviewer, achow101, raised two rounds of design feedback (avoid an optional-returning interface, then use util::Result for error propagation) and the author implemented both, most recently on 2026-08-19, with no unresolved objections. The bug is real but narrow: it only triggers when a wallet's selected or available unconfirmed inputs exceed roughly 500 ancestors. No dependencies block this PR, though it lists a passive file conflict with the unrelated #35511 CAmount refactor.
